candidate.title: TruSeq Nano
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq Nano library-preparation outline shown in the assigned Illumina panel, from double-stranded DNA to an amplified, indexed library ready for cluster generation. The panel does not identify the DNA's biological origin, an RNA-to-DNA conversion, a kit revision, or a sequencing read configuration. The two facing adaptor drawings are reagents incorporated at opposite fragment ends, not alternative methods. This is a schematic-level extraction, not a complete protocol.

states.label: Double-stranded DNA
features: Long DNA duplex; upstream biological source and preparation are not specified.

evidence.locator: Top substrate labelled 'Double-stranded DNA'

states.label: Fractionated, size-selected DNA duplex fragments
features: Shorter double-stranded fragments selected by size; no target size is specified.

evidence.locator: Upper arrow, 'Fractionate / Size select', and shorter duplex below

states.label: End-repaired, phosphorylated DNA duplex fragments
features: Aligned duplex ends after end repair.
P symbols at the upper-left and lower-right termini depict terminal phosphorylation.

evidence.locator: Second arrow, 'End repair / Phosphorylate', and duplex with P end symbols

states.label: A-overhang DNA duplex fragments
features: End-repaired fragments with A-labelled protruding termini at the lower-left and upper-right ends.

evidence.locator: Third arrow, 'A-overhang', and duplex with A end labels and retained P symbols

states.label: Forked, indexed DNA adaptors
features: The two facing adaptor drawings show opposite orientations for attachment at the two fragment ends, rather than alternative workflows.
T-labelled fragment-facing termini and P-labelled opposite termini are shown.
Forked arms carry labels P5, P7, Index 1 and Index 2; exact sequences are not supplied.

evidence.locator: Central plus sign and 'Add Adaptors'; two facing forked adaptors labelled T, P, P5, P7, Index 1 and Index 2

states.label: Adaptor-ligated DNA fragments
features: A central double-stranded DNA insert is flanked by attached forked adaptors.
The adaptor arms retain the depicted P5/P7 and Index 1/Index 2 annotations.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow labelled 'Adaptor ligation' and long duplex with forked adaptors attached at both ends

states.label: Amplified library product ready for cluster generation
features: Final linear duplex drawing retains the central DNA insert.
Terminal regions are labelled P5 and Index 2 on the left, Index 1 and P7 on the right.
The schematic ends before cluster generation or sequencing.
The DNA insert, rather than a separately generated probe product, carries the retained input-DNA sequence represented by the library.

evidence.rationale: The same central blue DNA duplex is retained as the insert while ends and adaptors change. The starting material is explicitly DNA; the panel shows no upstream biological source or conversion from RNA.

operations.label: Fractionate / Size select
operations.description: Convert the long DNA duplex into shorter fragments and retain size-selected DNA fragments.
operations.information_effect: The retained fragments carry portions of the starting DNA; size selection limits which fragments enter the library.

evidence.locator: Upper arrow, 'Fractionate / Size select', and shorter duplex below

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate
operations.description: Repair the selected fragment ends and introduce terminal phosphate groups, producing the aligned, P-marked duplex shown.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert is retained while its ends are prepared for subsequent adaptor attachment.

evidence.locator: Second arrow, 'End repair / Phosphorylate', and duplex with P end symbols

operations.label: A-overhang
operations.description: Add A-labelled protruding ends to the repaired, phosphorylated duplex while retaining the P-labelled opposite termini.
operations.information_effect: Changes fragment-end compatibility; the central DNA insert remains the carrier of target sequence.

evidence.locator: Third arrow, 'A-overhang', and duplex with A end labels and retained P symbols

operations.label: Add Adaptors / Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Add forked adaptors, drawn in opposite orientations, to the A-overhang fragments, as marked by the plus sign, and ligate them to produce a DNA insert flanked by forked adaptors. The addition caption and ligation arrow are represented as one joining operation with two material inputs.
operations.mechanism: The schematic juxtaposes fragment A overhangs with adaptor T termini and shows attached adaptors after the ligation arrow; enzymes and reaction conditions are not identified.
operations.information_effect: Physically associates adaptor-borne index and terminal regions with each retained DNA insert.

evidence.rationale: The plus sign presents adaptors as an added material; the ligation arrow leads to both adaptor orientations attached to one duplex. This supports a joining operation, not a workflow split or pooling of independent biological branches.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Denature and amplify the adaptor-ligated molecules. The forked adaptor depiction becomes a linear duplex library with P5 and Index 2 at the left and Index 1 and P7 at the right. No separate post-denaturation intermediate is drawn.
operations.information_effect: The amplified library carries retained input-DNA fragment sequences with physically linked index regions. Subsequent sequencing could recover sequence from those inserts, but the panel depicts no reads, biological source assignment, or index-to-sample map. Size selection and amplification do not establish complete or quantitative representation of the starting biological material.

evidence.locator: Bottom arrow, 'Denature and amplify', and 'Product ready for cluster generation'; final duplex labelled P5, Index 2, Index 1, P7

evidence.rationale: Because the insert remains DNA from the size-selected input fragments, its sequence is the biological information carried forward. The index labels establish linked index regions, while the endpoint explicitly stops before cluster generation; no sequencing data or biological measurement is shown. Selection and amplification preclude treating the drawing alone as evidence for complete or quantitative representation.
